title: EXCISE: Locating and Excising Distracting Sentences in Medical Question Answering
abstract: arXiv:2610.35558v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Language models are increasingly considered for clinical decision support, where their answers should be grounded in clinical evidence and remain robust to irrelevant information. Prior work shows that a single irrelevant sentence can lower the accuracy of medical models, but not where inside the model its effect can be removed, or how to do so without knowing which sentence it is. We find that blocking attention to a known distractor restores the answer, whereas head masking can suppress correct answers. We also show that the model's hidden states mark the distractor as the sentence that least fits the case even when the model follows it. To remove a distractor's effect without knowing which sentence it is, we propose EXCISE, an inference-time method that blocks the sentence most influencing the answer, but only if the model's hidden states mark it as inconsistent with the case. On MedQA-TD (MedQA with Targeted Distractors), a benchmark

translated_title: EXCISE：在医学问答中定位并切除干扰性句子
translated_abstract: 语言模型越来越多地被考虑用于临床决策支持，其答案应当基于临床证据，并对无关信息保持鲁棒性。先前的研究表明，单个无关句子即可降低医学模型的准确性，但其影响在模型内部何处能够被消除，以及在不明确是哪个句子的前提下如何消除这种影响，仍属未知。我们发现，阻断对已知干扰句的注意力可以恢复正确答案，而单纯的注意力头掩蔽则可能抑制正确答案。我们还发现，模型的隐藏状态会将干扰句标记为最不符合病例的句子，即使模型实际上遵循了该句子。为了在不明确是哪个句子的情况下消除干扰句的影响，我们提出了EXCISE，这是一种推理时方法，它会阻断对答案影响最大的句子，但前提是模型的隐藏状态将其标记为与病例不一致。在MedQA-TD（带有目标干扰项的MedQA）基准上，……
tldr: 提出推理时方法EXCISE，利用模型隐藏状态识别与病例不一致的句子并阻断其对答案的影响，从而在不需预先定位干扰句的情况下提升医学问答的鲁棒性。
en_tdlr: EXCISE is an inference-time method that blocks the sentence most influencing the model's answer only when hidden states mark it as inconsistent with the case, restoring robustness to distracting sentences in medical question answering without knowing which sentence is the distractor.
